root_cause.text: The `tegra124_emc_prepare_timing_change` function in the Tegra124 EMC driver used reversed logic when checking bit A0 of the EMRS register (`emc_mode_1`), incorrectly identifying DLL as enabled when the bit is high rather than low.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff replaces `else if (timing->emc_mode_1 & 0x1)` with `else if (!(timing->emc_mode_1 & 0x1))` to set `dll_change = DLL_CHANGE_ON`, and the commit message explains that "DLL is enabled if bit A0 is low. Fix the check."

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch diff replaces `else if (timing->emc_mode_1 & 0x1)` with `else if (!(timing->emc_mode_1 & 0x1))` to set `dll_change = DLL_CHANGE_ON`, and the commit message explains that "DLL is enabled if bit A0 is low. Fix the check."

intent_record.intent_summary: Correct the DLL state change logic by inverting the check on the EMC mode register bit to properly identify when the DLL is being enabled or disabled.
intent_record.what: Inverted the conditional check in the else-if statement from 'timing->emc_mode_1 & 0x1' to '!(timing->emc_mode_1 & 0x1)'.
intent_record.how: Corrects the logic for determining DLL status changes during memory timing transitions, ensuring DLL_CHANGE_ON is selected when the DLL disable bit is cleared (0) and DLL_CHANGE_OFF is selected when it is set (1).

grouping_result.intent: Correct the DLL state change logic by inverting the check on the EMC mode register bit to properly identify when the DLL is being enabled or disabled.

relevance_review.reason: The group's core intent is to correct the DLL state change logic by inverting the check on the EMC mode register bit, which directly addresses the reversed logic vulnerability described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This statement checks if bit A0 of the EMRS register is set, but incorrectly associates a high bit (which means DLL is disabled) with enabling the DLL (DLL_CHANGE_ON) in the subsequent block, representing the reversed logic.
This statement incorrectly sets the DLL change state to ON when the EMRS register bit A0 is high (which actually means DLL is disabled).
This statement incorrectly sets the DLL change state to OFF when the EMRS register bit A0 is low (which actually means DLL is enabled).
